_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); oilfield services signals

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'We are a leading provider of drilling, formation evaluation, completion and production products and services to the worldwide oil and natural gas industry'; 'The primary driver of our business is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to exploring, and drilling for, and developing and producing oil and natural gas'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ forecasts of future oil and natural gas prices, future economic growth and hydrocarbon demand and estimates of future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed' ; 'In addition, demand for hydrocarbons could be impacted by environmental regulation targeting reduction of greenhouse gas emissions including the cost for Carbon Capture and Sequestration' (its own FY2007 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'We are a leading provider of drilling, formation evaluation, completion and production products and services to the worldwide oil and natural gas industry'; 'The primary driver of our business is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to exploring, and drilling for, and developing and producing oil and natural gas'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ forecasts of future oil and natural gas prices, future economic growth and hydrocarbon demand and estimates of future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed' ; 'In addition, demand for hydrocarbons could be impacted by environmental regulation targeting reduction of greenhouse gas emissions including the cost for Carbon Capture and Sequestration' (its own FY2007 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B -0.02x; -69% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.80; conservative 2yr +431%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -26.0%/yr (worst year FY99-FY08, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +17.0%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +59.4%/yr (FY99-FY08 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +298.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY99-FY08); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BHI (retrospective, 2009-02-13) ◉ BUY — Ratio B -0.02x (-29.3% downside to Bear $43 / +1301.1% upside to Bull $466) | Adj composite 2.85 vs market 1.05: gap +1.80 [UNDERVALUED] | -69% above the EPP floor $106 (20x FY09E $5.30) | Conservative 2-yr case: +430.8% total (+215.4%/yr) | At 6.3x FY09E the 15% hurdle price $44 sits at or below the BASE case; North America revenue +24.5% and revenue outside North America +10.5% in Q4 2008, forward revenues +16.3% (no Q1 2009 revenue guide, Q4 2008 revenue as reported); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
